rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. Testing a simple RNA-only model with PCA (config_001) isolates the effect of RNA modality and basic encoding, providing a reference point to compare multimodal or image-only approaches later. This balances exploration of single-modality performance with the need to understand baseline accuracy before testing more complex configurations.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA achieves 0.48 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile RNA-only with avgpool aggregation, which directly compares profile setting changes while keeping RNA encoder and other factors constant. It clarifies whether multiprofile configuration improves performance, addressing a key design choice with minimal additional complexity.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile (config_001). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (config_003) further improves accuracy, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of the multiprofile RNA-only direction with exploration of a key design choice (aggregation).

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.590 accuracy) is the strongest so far. This experiment tests combining RNA and image data (multimodal) with the same multiprofile and avgpool settings to determine if multimodal fusion improves accuracy. It isolates the effect of adding image modality while maintaining the proven RNA encoding and aggregation strategy.

Existing evidence shows config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6186). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scvi_n200 (a more advanced model) while keeping other components identical could further improve performance. This balances exploitation of the successful multimodal/multiprofile setup with exploration of a key design choice (RNA encoder), which may yield significant gains without changing multiple factors simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models (like config_030) outperform rna_only and image_only baselines. This experiment tests whether changing fusion method from concat to weighted in config_030's successful setup improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It builds on the strongest current configuration while exploring a critical design choice with potential for incremental gains.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion achieves 0.677 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method to transformer (while keeping weighted fusion) could further improve performance, isolating the effect of aggregation strategy. It is the best next step as it builds on the current top-performing configuration and explores a critical design choice with minimal changes.

The existing evidence shows that config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a more powerful image encoder) while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion consistent. This isolates the impact of the image encoder choice, which is critical for multimodal performance. It balances exploitation (building on prior success) and exploration (testing a key design choice with high potential impact).

The existing evidence shows that using 'imagenet_vit_l' image encoder with 'transformer' aggregation and 'weighted' fusion (e.g., config_039) achieves high accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests replacing 'scvi_n200' RNA encoder with 'scgpt' (a more advanced model) while keeping other components the same. It clarifies whether scgpt's capabilities further improve performance, balancing exploration of RNA encoder choices with the strong foundation of existing multimodal settings.

The existing evidence shows that config_039 (scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy of 0.7249. This experiment tests whether using concat fusion instead of weighted fusion with the same RNA/image encoders and transformer aggregation could yield comparable or better performance. It clarifies the impact of fusion method on model performance, which is critical for optimizing multimodal integration. Since this is the final experiment, testing this configuration directly compares two key fusion strategies in the most promising architecture.
